claim: hoisting the warm membership lock out of the per-furnace loop is result-identical and faster on every measured fixture
cause: is_warm locks a mutex on every call, so a loop over N furnaces took N locks per tick. Measured 5758us for 400 idle furnaces, about 14us each, which is lock cost rather than comparison cost.
equivalence: the membership test is unchanged; only the number of lock acquisitions changes. Same div_euclid(16), same set.
measurement: HEAD baseline, same fixtures, runner and release build, 3 processes each. Idle 400 furnaces: tick x1.16, furnace stage x1.60. Active furnaces: tick x1.17, stage x1.43. All other fixtures x0.99-1.03. Whole-process CPU 0.2722-0.2733s -> 0.2660-0.2696s.
regression_found_and_fixed: without an early return the furnace-less fixtures regressed from 27us to 36us per tick (x0.78) because the lock was taken unconditionally. Measurement caught it.
near_miss: a first attempt hoisted five loops at once and held the same mutex while still calling is_hot inside, which would deadlock on a non-reentrant mutex. Reverted and done one block at a time.
remaining: 20 call sites still lock per item, in crop growth, bobbers, pearls, xp, drops, arrows, primed tnt, mobs and plugin cells. Each needs the same treatment, one block at a time, verifying no re-entry.
measurement_limit: this fixture only; not a whole-server or vanilla-comparison result
tests: 32 passed, 0 failed, 1 explicitly ignored, serial and at 8 threads
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force
provenance_note: results-before was measured before the air-supply commit, so it also differs in ['src/main.rs', 'src/tick_tests.rs']. Only src/main.rs differs between the two measurements, which is the change under test.
